sections.html:
Kingwood is the seat of Preston County, which borders Pennsylvania to the north and Maryland to the east. The county has about 651 square miles, split by the Cheat River into two sections. Population was about 34,200 in 2020 and is estimated at 34,004 for 2025. Home ownership runs 80.7 percent, and the median home value is $128,800.

Besides Kingwood the county has nine towns: Albright, Brandonville, Bruceton Mills, Masontown, Newburg, Reedsville, Rowlesburg, Terra Alta and Tunnelton. Eight old magisterial districts were merged into five numbered districts in the 1990s. Part of the county sits within the Morgantown area, and Interstate 68 across the north makes the drive to Monongalia County and Maryland easier, which helps with demand for houses near the highway.

Preston County is known for hard winters, so a house's cold-weather condition deserves attention from a buyer. Terra Alta holds the state's record monthly snowfall, 104 inches in January 1977.

  • Keep records of roof, insulation and heating work, since a buyer or lender may ask for them.
  • If the house will sit empty over the winter, arrange for someone to check it after cold snaps.
  • Keep the tax ticket and insurance current while the house is unoccupied, so no delinquency date passes unnoticed.

sections.h2: Old deeds and the 1869 courthouse fire
sections.html:
A fire in 1869 left a gap in the county's paper trail. An arsonist burned one of the courthouses that replaced the 1820s building in 1869, destroying most of the county records for 1818 to 1869.

That matters to anyone selling an old farm or a parcel with a long chain of title. Deeds from before 1869 may be missing from the courthouse, so a title search can lean on later deeds, surveys and the assessor's tax maps, and a title agent will want extra lead time to work through the gaps. If a parcel has been in a family for generations, start the paperwork early.

The Sheriff's Tax Office collects and the Preston County Assessor values the property. Both work out of the courthouse at 106 West Main Street in Kingwood.

Sheriff's Tax Office106 W Main Street, Kingwood, WV 26537304-329-0105
Assessor106 West Main Street, Room 101304-329-1220

Call the tax office before you go to confirm the suite. The county links an online tax inquiry and online payment through vendor sites, and the assessor offers tax maps, land records and a sales search through an online portal. Start from the county departments page, and bring a photo ID, your latest tax ticket and the deed or probate papers if you are dealing with an inherited house.

The state calendar governs here. Your ticket should arrive on or after July 15, and the two installments fall on September 1 and March 1.

  • Pay ahead of either installment date to keep a 2.5 percent discount.
  • A first half still owing on October 1 is delinquent, and so is a second half on April 1.
  • Interest on delinquent amounts is 9 percent a year.

By September 10 the sheriff adds any parcel still delinquent on September 1 to a second list. Unredeemed liens then go to the State Auditor on October 31. Up to that point you redeem through the sheriff by paying the tax, interest and charges, which include $25 for the list and $10 per mailed notice.

Schools take the largest slice. Preston County levied $23,779,702 across all purposes: $13,997,924 for schools, $8,244,991 for county purposes, $1,404,231 for municipal purposes and $132,556 for the state.

Real estate made up $13,001,997 of that. Homes lived in by their owners (Class II) accounted for $7,981,104, property outside municipalities (Class III) for $3,562,990 and property inside municipalities (Class IV) for $1,457,904. The state taxes Class II at twice the Class I rate, and Classes III and IV at four times.

The window is in winter, and the county commission hears your case in its role as the board of equalization and review.

Sessions start by February 1. Once February 15 passes the board may close, though it has to be done by the last day of the month. Reductions and corrections are within its power, and it resets anything not at 60 percent of true value. Before an increase you get five days of written notice. Miss the meeting and you forfeit that year's correction, except for the Office of Tax Appeals route. Your evidence needs to show your position is more likely right than not.

Homeowners who are 65 or older, or certified permanently and totally disabled, and who pass the residency test, can exempt $20,000 of assessed value.

The exemption follows the home the owner lived in on July 1 and takes effect the next tax year. Passing the house on by deed or will ends it at the following July 1 unless the new owner qualifies, so heirs ought to ask the assessor what the next bill will look like.

sections.h2: Steps for selling with tax owing
sections.html:
Anyone with an open balance can work through the same few steps. Phone the Sheriff's Tax Office on 304-329-0105 and request the amount owed for each year, including anything that has gone delinquent. Call the Assessor on 304-329-1220 to confirm the class on your parcel and whether a homestead exemption is on file. Then ask the title company to start the search early, particularly for an old farm where records from before 1869 may be missing.

If the house has stood empty through a winter, plan to show the buyer's inspector that heat, roof and insurance were kept up. A cash buyer will buy the house in its present condition, and the title company still pays the taxes from proceeds, so you do not need to finish repairs or chase down missing paperwork first. Say so up front when you call, and the cash buyer can plan the closing around the next due date.

Back tax gets paid from proceeds or ahead of closing, after which the deed is recorded with the county clerk. The Sheriff's Tax Office can quote a payoff for each year, and the title company can run the chain of title.

Transfer tax comes to $1.10 per $500 (the county has kept it since July 1, 2025), a county add-on of 55 cents per $500 unless the commission raised it, and a $20 fee. Sellers cover it unless the buyer takes the deed with the tax unpaid.

faqs.q: When are Preston County property taxes due?
faqs.a: One half is due September 1 and one March 1. A 2.5 percent discount rewards paying early, and halves left unpaid are delinquent October 1 and April 1.

faqs.q: Where do I pay property tax in Preston County?
faqs.a: Pay at the Sheriff's Tax Office at 106 West Main Street in Kingwood, phone 304-329-0105, or online through the county's vendor link. Call ahead to confirm the suite.

faqs.q: Is there an assessment appeal deadline in Preston County?
faqs.a: The county commission meets as the board of equalization and review by February 1 and finishes by the end of February.

faqs.q: What happens if my Preston County taxes go unpaid?
faqs.a: Interest of 9 percent a year starts at delinquency. A parcel still delinquent on September 1 goes on the sheriff's second list, and its lien can be certified to the State Auditor October 31.

faqs.q: Do old Preston County deeds exist from before 1869?
faqs.a: Many may not. An arson fire in 1869 destroyed most county records from 1818 to 1869, so a title search on an old parcel can depend on later deeds and surveys.
